<!-- Generated by SiteFrames render from Tests/Api/round2-parity.json. -->
I use the same domain names for cmdlet parameters, C# configuration and fluent calls. PowerShell keeps numeric duration parameters with units and default-off switches; C# keeps TimeSpan values and Boolean properties.

The contract covers **89 commands**, **1034 parameters** and **333 reachable public types**. The metadata gate checks names, types, sets, positions, defaults, nullability and member paths. Rendering and triplet tests check behavior.

Show-ConsoleTable displays tables. Show-Console -View List and Show-Console -View Tree display lists and trees. Read-* returns answers; New-ConsoleForm/Menu defines a question workflow; Show-ConsoleApp runs a persistent reactive application.

PowerShell exports use individual parameters, for example `Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Html -Width 100`. C# export calls accept typed ExportOptions configuration.

Callback properties use `.Configure(item => item.Action = …)`. C# invokes a delegate-valued property before considering an extension with that name; Configure assigns the callback without invoking it.

## Fluent construction and nesting

Ui is the fluent entry point: New-ConsolePanel becomes Ui.Panel(), named settings stay in the chain, and nested Content uses c.Panel(p => …). Initializers retain constructors. Factories accept no positional configuration; the recorded primary inputs below are the only exceptions. Chart, Progress and kind-selected inputs materialize their existing typed options through the shared Build operation.

Literal text uses `Ui.Text(text)` or `c.Text(text)`; PowerShell `-Markup` uses `Ui.Markup(markup)` or `c.Markup(markup)`. Boolean properties named IsX keep that property in initializers and use `.X()` / `.X(false)` in fluent chains. Adjacent configuration stays in one chain.

Operation options use a typed configure callback, for example `ConsoleRun.ForEachAsync(items, work, o => o.ThrottleLimit(2).Title("Build"))`. The operation creates fresh defaults, invokes the callback once and delegates to its existing implementation. `Ui.Options<T>()` is removed.

## Parameter-set mappings

A structural parameter set can select a different request model. The metadata gate checks these mappings separately and includes both update requests in its public-member coverage.

## Individual member decisions

Native host hooks, runtime models and equivalent representations are listed individually. These decisions do not exempt a namespace or hide newly added options.

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Overview.OverviewOptions.ProbeTimeout</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Per-provider cooperative timeout policy belongs to the C# overview host; PowerShell exposes the caller collection budget.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleOverview -BudgetMilliseconds to bound the whole collection.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Values.ShapeOptions.Separator</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Controls inline collection text in a custom C# shaper; PowerShell uses its standard collection presentation.</td><td>PowerShell uses its canonical PSObject/member shaping and explicit Property/Culture selection.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Values.ShapeOptions.TypeNames</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: PowerShell uses PSObject.TypeNames; native C# models may supply additional type names.</td><td>PowerShell uses its canonical PSObject/member shaping and explicit Property/Culture selection.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Values.ShapeOptions.Unwrap</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: PowerShell owns wrapper unwrapping; this delegate is for native C# wrapper types.</td><td>PowerShell uses its canonical PSObject/member shaping and explicit Property/Culture selection.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.BasePath</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: PowerShell supplies its current filesystem provider path for source diagnostics; C# hosts choose their own base path.</td><td>Use Show-Console’s representation/property options or the public ConsoleHostViews adapter for C# PowerShell hosts.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.DetailsHint</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The PowerShell adapter generates the native Get-Error hint; C# hosts supply wording for their own error-detail route.</td><td>Use Show-Console’s representation/property options or the public ConsoleHostViews adapter for C# PowerShell hosts.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.Shape</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: PowerShell owns PSObject shaping and runspace selectors; native C# hosts supply their own ShapeOptions.</td><td>Use Show-Console’s representation/property options or the public ConsoleHostViews adapter for C# PowerShell hosts.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.Sources</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native member-source implementations are the AOT/C# extension point; cmdlets install the canonical PSObject source.</td><td>Use Show-Console’s representation/property options or the public ConsoleHostViews adapter for C# PowerShell hosts.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Dashboard.CompactSummary</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A C# embedding host may supply a separate compact widget; PowerShell uses the dashboard’s normal compact summary.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleDashboard and the normal adaptive dashboard layout.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Dashboard.MinimumSize</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Controls an embedded C# dashboard’s compact-mode threshold; the PowerShell host keeps its supported adaptive threshold.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleDashboard and the normal adaptive dashboard layout.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ExceptionView.BasePath</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: PowerShell supplies its current provider path for source links; C# hosts supply their own source root.</td><td>Use Show-Console -View Error with its source/stack flags.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ExceptionView.DetailsHint</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: PowerShell generates its own native Get-Error hint; C# embedding hosts supply another detail action.</td><td>Use Show-Console -View Error with its source/stack flags.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Histogram.EdgeFormat</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: This synchronous native formatter is called by the render thread; a PowerShell script block cannot safely run there.</td><td>Use numeric bucket Edges and Unit; custom C# columns may format bucket labels.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.InspectorView.Presentation</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A C# host can pin a static inspector’s clock/time zone; PowerShell uses the owning host’s current value presentation.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleObject’s standard inspector presentation.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Lane.Order</code></td><td>RuntimeOwned: The Lanes collection assigns insertion order; PowerShell record order is pipeline order.</td><td>Supply records in the required order to New-ConsoleLanes.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.RecordView.IndentWidth</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: C# embedded records can pin indentation; the PowerShell list view uses its standard two-cell nesting layout.</td><td>Use Show-Console -View List and its Property/Depth/ShowEmpty/Culture controls.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.RecordView.MaxLabelFraction</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: C# embedded records can pin the label/value ratio; the PowerShell list view keeps its adaptive label policy.</td><td>Use Show-Console -View List and its Property/Depth/ShowEmpty/Culture controls.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.RecordView.Summary</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A directly composed C# record header may include a separate summary; the PowerShell list view derives its record headings from the input.</td><td>Use Show-Console -View List and its Property/Depth/ShowEmpty/Culture controls.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ShellPrompt.Branch</code></td><td>RuntimeOwned: PowerShell supplies its cached Git branch; a C# shell host supplies its own repository state.</td><td>Enable-ConsoleFormatting -Feature Prompt obtains this data from the owning PowerShell session.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ShellPrompt.Succeeded</code></td><td>RuntimeOwned: PowerShell supplies the last native/pipeline outcome; a C# shell host supplies its own command result.</td><td>Enable-ConsoleFormatting -Feature Prompt obtains this data from the owning PowerShell session.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.Alignment</code></td><td>EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock and RichText share alignment behavior; PowerShell exposes Alignment on its canonical RichText result.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.Role</code></td><td>EquivalentRepresentation: TextBlock stores a block role; PowerShell applies the same Role through RichText’s base style.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleText -Text/-Markup/-Role/-Alignment/-Overflow; its RichText result is also a widget.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeHierarchyOptions.Identity</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A native graph identity delegate supports custom/AOT C# nodes; the PowerShell hierarchy adapter owns wrapped-object identity.</td><td>Use the canonical PSObject identity and bounded tree traversal.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.LogViewport.Capacity</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The retained log viewport wraps the existing bounded LogRegion without adding a second log constructor cmdlet.</td><td>Create LogViewport in PowerShell or C#, configure Capacity, and embed it in Show-ConsoleApp.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.LogViewport.ScrollOffset</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The retained log viewport wraps the existing bounded LogRegion without adding a second log constructor cmdlet.</td><td>Create LogViewport in PowerShell or C#, configure ScrollOffset, and embed it in Show-ConsoleApp.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.LogViewport.HorizontalOffset</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The retained log viewport wraps the existing bounded LogRegion without adding a second log constructor cmdlet.</td><td>Create LogViewport in PowerShell or C#, configure HorizontalOffset, and embed it in Show-ConsoleApp.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.AxisLabel</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: An axis caption describes the supplied numeric model; automatic chart input does not infer that caption.</td><td>Set AxisLabel on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.IsHealthy</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The matrix attention list needs an application-supplied health policy rather than inferring health from labels.</td><td>Assign IsHealthy in a native Matrix builder and pass the resulting widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShowLegend</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A matrix legend summarizes supplied cross-tab observations; automatic object views have no matrix legend.</td><td>Set ShowLegend on Matrix before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathSet.MaxHops</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The accepted chain length is a budget for an explicitly supplied path model.</td><td>Set MaxHops on PathSet before adding chains and passing the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TableRowRole.AsciiMarker</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The reduced-tier marker is part of an explicit whole-row role, independent of per-column role rules.</td><td>Set AsciiMarker on TableRowRole and supply that role to native Table.AddRow.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TableRowRole.Tone</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A whole-row semantic tone is independent of the ordinary column presentation policy.</td><td>Set Tone on TableRowRole and supply that role to native Table.AddRow.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.CollapsedSummary</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A collapsed-node aggregate requires a typed application callback and does not enumerate descendants itself.</td><td>Assign CollapsedSummary in a native Tree builder and pass the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeHierarchyOptions.CollapsedSummary</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: An object aggregate for a collapsed node is application-specific and must not trigger another child traversal.</td><td>Supply CollapsedSummary through TreeHierarchyOptions when calling TreeHierarchy.Add; New-ConsoleTree retains its bounded object traversal.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeHierarchyOptions.IsIncomplete</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Knowing whether application-owned children are incomplete requires a pure application callback.</td><td>Supply IsIncomplete through TreeHierarchyOptions passed to TreeHierarchy.Add; use MaxItems, MaxNodes and Depth for ordinary PowerShell traversal budgets.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.Identity</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Stable graph identity is supplied independently of a node label or display value.</td><td>Set Identity when building native TreeNode instances and pass the tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.Reference</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A node reference records an explicit cycle or previously shown node rather than deriving it from text.</td><td>Set Reference on a native TreeNode with an identity-aware tree builder.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.ReferenceSummary</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Reference wording belongs to the explicitly identified native node.</td><td>Set ReferenceSummary on a native TreeNode before showing the tree.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.Values</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Keyed value cells require the explicit native tree column schema.</td><td>Populate TreeNode.Values to match Tree.ValueColumns and pass the tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.AsciiListDirection</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The reduced-tier connector belongs to an explicitly supplied directional cross-tab.</td><td>Set AsciiListDirection with ListDirection on a native Matrix, then pass it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ColumnAxisCaption</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The column-axis caption names the supplied matrix dimension rather than an inferred object property.</td><td>Set ColumnAxisCaption on a native Matrix before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.LegendLabels</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Application-supplied legend words describe matrix statuses without changing their semantics.</td><td>Populate Matrix.LegendLabels by StatusKind before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.LegendMarkers</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Literal legend markers belong to an explicit matrix and do not alter its cell statuses or counts.</td><td>Populate Matrix.LegendMarkers with ASCII-safe glyphs for all-tier output and pass the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ListDirection</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A directional connector describes the relationship between explicitly supplied row and column identities.</td><td>Set ListDirection and its AsciiListDirection alternative on a native Matrix, then pass it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.MissingLegendLabel</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: An absent observation needs application wording distinct from a supplied healthy result.</td><td>Set MissingLegendLabel on a native Matrix before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.RowAxisCaption</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The row-axis caption names the supplied matrix dimension rather than an inferred object property.</td><td>Set RowAxisCaption on a native Matrix before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.SelfLegendLabel</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The self-cell legend describes explicitly identified diagonal relationships.</td><td>Set SelfLegendLabel on a native Matrix before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.TruncateLabelsInMiddle</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Preserving both ends of an identity label is a native tree presentation choice.</td><td>Set TruncateLabelsInMiddle on the Tree returned by New-ConsoleTree before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.TruncateNotesInMiddle</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Preserving both ends of a detail or value note is independent of label truncation.</td><td>Set TruncateNotesInMiddle on a native Tree with node details or value columns before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.AsciiMarker</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The ASCII node marker is supplied independently of status semantics and the full-tier marker.</td><td>Set AsciiMarker on native TreeNode instances before passing their tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.BasicMarker</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A Basic-tier node marker can differ from both full Unicode and ASCII markers.</td><td>Set BasicMarker together with Marker and AsciiMarker on native TreeNode instances.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.Marker</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A literal node marker is application presentation rather than an inferred status.</td><td>Set Marker on native TreeNode instances and supply reduced-tier alternatives when needed.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.MarkerTone</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The marker tone can express application meaning independently of the node status and label style.</td><td>Set MarkerTone to a ThemeToken on native TreeNode instances before passing their tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.BarHeader</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The bar column caption belongs to a configured native chart.</td><td>Set BarHeader on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.BarWidth</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A fixed bar width is a native chart layout choice.</td><td>Set BarWidth on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.LabelHeader</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The label column caption describes the supplied chart identities.</td><td>Set LabelHeader on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.ShowTrack</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Showing unused bar capacity is a native chart presentation choice.</td><td>Set ShowTrack on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.SpanMissingValues</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Spanning an unavailable observation is an explicit native chart layout choice.</td><td>Set SpanMissingValues on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.ValueHeader</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The value column caption describes the supplied chart measure.</td><td>Set ValueHeader on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.BarChart.ValuePresenter</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A custom measure presenter belongs to the native chart composition.</td><td>Assign ValuePresenter on the BarChart returned by New-ConsoleChart -Type Bar.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ConsoleViewFrame.Blocks</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Body blocks form an explicitly composed embedded view.</td><td>Add native widgets to ConsoleViewFrame.Blocks and pass the frame to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ConsoleViewFrame.Footer</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The footer is an optional widget in an explicitly composed embedded view.</td><td>Set ConsoleViewFrame.Footer and pass the frame to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ConsoleViewFrame.Headline</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The headline is an optional widget beneath an embedded view header.</td><td>Set ConsoleViewFrame.Headline and pass the frame to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FactFlow.Parts</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Fact entries are markup fragments supplied by an embedded view builder.</td><td>Populate FactFlow.Parts and pass the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FactFlow.Role</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A fact tone is supplied by its native presentation builder.</td><td>Set FactFlow.Role before passing the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>

<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Legend.Entries</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Legend entries describe the application-supplied meanings of an explicit view.</td><td>Populate Legend.Entries and pass the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.AdditionalLegendEntries</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Extra legend words describe application-supplied matrix annotations.</td><td>Populate Matrix.AdditionalLegendEntries before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.CellNote</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A cell annotation describes the supplied matrix values.</td><td>Set Matrix.CellNote before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.InlineAxes</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Inline axes are an explicit matrix presentation choice.</td><td>Set Matrix.InlineAxes before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.LegendRoles</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Legend tones belong to the application-supplied matrix status meanings.</td><td>Populate Matrix.LegendRoles before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.MinCellWidth</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The minimum matrix cell width is a native layout constraint.</td><td>Set Matrix.MinCellWidth before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShortColumnAxisCaption</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A compact column caption is supplied independently of the full matrix caption.</td><td>Set Matrix.ShortColumnAxisCaption with ColumnAxisCaption on a native Matrix.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShortRowAxisCaption</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A compact row caption is supplied independently of the full matrix caption.</td><td>Set Matrix.ShortRowAxisCaption with RowAxisCaption on a native Matrix.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Matrix.ShowLegendCounts</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Legend counts are an explicit matrix summary presentation choice.</td><td>Set Matrix.ShowLegendCounts before passing the matrix to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathHop.Bold</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Emphasis belongs to an explicitly supplied native path hop.</td><td>Set PathHop.Bold on a hop in a PathSet before passing the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathHop.Role</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A hop tone expresses application-supplied relationship meaning.</td><td>Set PathHop.Role on a hop in a PathSet before passing the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.PathSet.CompactBranches</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Compact connectors are an explicit native path layout choice.</td><td>Set PathSet.CompactBranches before passing the widget to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Maximum</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The gauge maximum is supplied by the application alongside its score.</td><td>Set ScoreGauge.Maximum and pass the gauge to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Parts</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Score components are labels and values supplied by the application.</td><td>Populate ScoreGauge.Parts and pass the gauge to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Role</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The finding tone is supplied by the application rather than computed by the gauge.</td><td>Set ScoreGauge.Role and pass the gauge to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Value</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The gauge displays an application-supplied score without calculating it.</td><td>Set ScoreGauge.Value and pass the gauge to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ScoreGauge.Width</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A fixed gauge width is an explicit native layout choice.</td><td>Set ScoreGauge.Width and pass the gauge to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TableRowRole.MarkerTone</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A row marker tone is supplied independently of the row label and status.</td><td>Set MarkerTone on a native TableRowRole used by the table builder.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.CompactGuides</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Compact guides are an explicit native hierarchy layout choice.</td><td>Set CompactGuides on the Tree returned by New-ConsoleTree before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.Tree.ValuePlacement</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Value placement selects the layout of explicitly supplied tree value columns.</td><td>Set ValuePlacement on the Tree returned by New-ConsoleTree before passing it to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TextBlock.WrapSeparator</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Separator-aware wrapping is a layout option on an explicit TextBlock; New-ConsoleText returns RichText and does not expose this option.</td><td>Construct a TextBlock, set WrapSeparator, and pass the widget to Show-Console or use it as a ConsoleViewFrame footer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.MeasureBareLabel</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: This per-node option includes a bare node in measurement of explicitly configured tree value columns.</td><td>Set MeasureBareLabel on a bare TreeNode in an explicit tree with ValueColumns, then pass the tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.Bare</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A bare node omits the ordinary hierarchy decoration in an explicit tree.</td><td>Set Bare on a native TreeNode before passing its tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.TreeNode.TruncateLabelInMiddle</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Preserving both ends of one node label is a per-node layout choice.</td><td>Set TruncateLabelInMiddle on a native TreeNode before passing its tree to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.Facts</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Header facts are supplied by an embedded view builder.</td><td>Populate ViewHeader.Facts and pass the header or its ConsoleViewFrame to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.State</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The header state is supplied by the application and can contain status markup.</td><td>Set ViewHeader.State and pass the header or its ConsoleViewFrame to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.Streaming</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: An open-stream header describes collection rather than a final verdict.</td><td>Set ViewHeader.Streaming in a native streaming-header builder.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHeader.Title</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The embedded view title is literal application-supplied context.</td><td>Set ViewHeader.Title and pass the header or its ConsoleViewFrame to Show-Console.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHint.Columns</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Hidden column names are supplied by the view layout owner.</td><td>Populate ViewHint.Columns and use the hint as a native view footer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.ViewHint.MoreRows</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The omitted-row count is supplied by the view collection owner.</td><td>Set ViewHint.MoreRows and use the hint as a native view footer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.ColorDepth</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Export rendering creates its own fixed profile from ColorDepth; the cmdlet deliberately keeps TrueColor rather than inheriting the terminal target depth.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame for its normal artifact profile; native exporters can set ExportOptions.ColorDepth explicitly.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Culture</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A native artifact renderer can pin numeric/date culture independently of its host; the cmdlet leaves Culture null and uses the current culture.</td><td>Select the PowerShell current culture before rendering, or set ExportOptions.Culture in native export code.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.DarkTheme</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native HTML/SVG callers may inject a custom dark ITheme; the cmdlet exposes only the ExportTheme preset selector and leaves the custom theme unset.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Theme Auto/Dark/Light/HighContrast; supply DarkTheme through native ExportOptions for custom palettes.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Elapsed</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A native snapshot renderer can pin the session clock for spinners and header clocks; fresh widget exports keep the zero-time default.</td><td>Export a captured frame/session for its rendered state, or set ExportOptions.Elapsed in a deterministic native renderer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Fragment</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: HTML embedding hosts can request a styled fragment rather than a complete page; Export-ConsoleFrame produces its self-contained document contract.</td><td>Consume the full HTML from Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Html, or request Fragment in a native HTML exporter.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Glyphs</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Export rendering uses the option's Full glyph tier independently of the ambient terminal target; the cmdlet keeps that artifact default.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame with full export glyphs, or configure ExportOptions.Glyphs in a native exporter.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.IndividualTextElements</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native SVG consumers with limited text models can request one element per grapheme; ordinary SVG export keeps compact text and the graphics provider selects its required representation internally.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Format Svg/Png for the supported serializers; native SVG integration can set IndividualTextElements.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.LightTheme</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native dual-theme exports may inject a separate light ITheme; the cmdlet keeps the built-in light palette instead of an arbitrary theme object.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Theme Auto or Light; native ExportOptions.LightTheme supports a custom light palette.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.LineHeight</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native artifact hosts can alter the font-to-cell-height ratio; the cmdlet keeps the 1.2 geometry while exposing font size and cell dimensions.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame -FontSize/-Width/-Height; set LineHeight in native ExportOptions for custom cell metrics.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.ExportOptions.Padding</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native page/image embedding can set its pixel margin; the cmdlet keeps the 12-pixel frame margin and lets raster presets choose their composition.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleFrame -Preset for the supported raster composition, or set ExportOptions.Padding in native embedding code.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Culture</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recording renders may pin numeric/date culture; PlaybackOptions leaves Culture null and uses the current culture.</td><td>Select the PowerShell current culture before exporting, or supply RecordingExportOptions.Culture from a native renderer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.CustomTheme</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recording exporters can supply one custom ITheme; the cmdlet deliberately accepts the built-in Theme presets and leaves CustomTheme unset.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleRecording -Theme Dark/Light/HighContrast, or native RecordingExportOptions.CustomTheme for an injected palette.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.FontSize</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recording serializers can set natural-size typography; the cmdlet keeps the 14-pixel recording font. MaxFontSize is a raster fitting ceiling, not this setting.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleRecording -Preset/-MaxFontSize for raster fitting; configure FontSize in native recording export options for natural-size typography.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Glyphs</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recording rendering can choose a glyph tier; the cmdlet keeps Full glyphs rather than exposing another artifact-profile override.</td><td>Use the standard Export-ConsoleRecording artifact profile, or set RecordingExportOptions.Glyphs in native export code.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.LineHeight</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recording serializers can alter the cell-height multiplier; the cmdlet retains the shared 1.2 geometry.</td><td>Use the supported recording dimensions and raster presets; native RecordingExportOptions.LineHeight controls custom cell metrics.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Loop</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: This Boolean controls SVG animation repetition. The cmdlet keeps SVG looping enabled; LoopCount controls the separate GIF/APNG graphics job and is not this property.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleRecording -LoopCount for raster animation; set RecordingExportOptions.Loop for native SVG repetition policy.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.MaxFrames</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: This is the export sampler's regular-frame cap of 900; Show-ConsoleReplay -MaxFrames governs the different in-terminal player job.</td><td>Use Export-ConsoleRecording -FramesPerSecond for export sampling frequency; native RecordingExportOptions.MaxFrames controls the export cap.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Padding</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recording page/image hosts can change the pixel margin; PlaybackOptions retains the 12-pixel export margin.</td><td>Use recording raster presets for the supported layout, or set RecordingExportOptions.Padding in native artifact embedding.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Export.RecordingExportOptions.Timestamp</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native asciicast serialization can override the optional header timestamp; the cmdlet does not add an export-time timestamp override.</td><td>Keep the recording's source metadata through Export-ConsoleRecording, or set Timestamp when a native caller creates an asciicast header.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.Choice.Tag</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native selection hosts can attach metadata separate from Choice.Value. PowerShell selectors retain the chosen source object and return its value without a separate Tag projection.</td><td>Keep metadata on the original PowerShell choice object; native Choice.Tag remains available to a typed selection host.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.ConsoleAppOptions.Live</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A native app host can inject its full-screen live-session configuration; Show-ConsoleApp owns the session and maps input, capture, profile and theme through Interactive instead.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleApp -InputSource/-Capture/-Profile/-Theme/-Mode; native ConsoleAppOptions.Live configures a custom session host.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.FormOptions.AfterSubmit</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A native full-screen form can run a MenuContext dashboard callback before leaving its screen. Read-ConsoleForm returns submitted answers and does not run another work callback inside that screen.</td><td>Read the form result, then invoke the requested PowerShell work or dashboard; native FormOptions.AfterSubmit retains in-screen composition.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.Labels</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native prompt hosts can inject a customized PromptLabels instance. PowerShell resolves the built-in catalogue from the active profile language rather than accepting a replacement label object.</td><td>Select CONSOLEMONSTER_LANGUAGE or the UI culture; set each question's Title/Description for its own wording.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.LineConsole</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native embeddings can inject line-oriented input/output devices. PSInteractive chooses the owning PowerShell host UI for Line/Accessible modes, including remoting and ISE.</td><td>Use the command's -Mode Line/Accessible; native InteractiveOptions.LineConsole can supply a custom device.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.MaxInlineHeight</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native prompt hosts can cap the inline screen independently of the detected terminal height. PowerShell keeps the shared automatic prompt-height policy.</td><td>Use supported PageSize/Height options on the specific input where exposed, or set MaxInlineHeight in a native prompt host.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.NonInteractive</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can explicitly disable prompting. <tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.InteractiveOptions.Target</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native callers can override one prompt's terminal target. PowerShell scopes its target through Terminal.Use and keeps input/capture overrides on the high-level app command.</td><td>Use Use-ConsoleTarget -Target for the scoped target, or Show-ConsoleApp -InputSource/-Capture for explicit app devices.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.Group</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native key-map hosts choose the heading under which a binding is listed; PowerShell menu/app commands use the shared host-generated action groups.</td><td>Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.InFooter</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native key-map hosts can suppress one binding in the footer while keeping it in the key map; PowerShell keeps the shared footer-selection policy.</td><td>Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.KeyText</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native bindings can replace the displayed chord text with a glyph or custom caption; PowerShell actions keep their actual Hotkey and generated key hints.</td><td>Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.KeyBinding.Order</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native key-map hosts set the footer retention priority of a binding; PowerShell keeps the shared ordering of its generated input and command bindings.</td><td>Use the input/menu defaults or New-ConsoleCommand -Hotkey/-Label for supported actions; configure this field on a native KeyBinding for a custom key map.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.Menu.CommandProviders</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native menu applications can add ICommandProvider implementations to discover palette actions. The PowerShell parent accepts explicit menu definitions rather than arbitrary provider implementations.</td><td>Declare actions with New-ConsoleMenuItem and compose the menu; a native Menu.CommandProviders collection supports provider-driven discovery.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.Menu.KeyBindings</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native menu applications can register arbitrary synchronous KeyBinding actions. PowerShell menu callbacks use the owning runspace adapters and menu-item hotkeys.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleMenuItem -Hotkey/-Action; native hosts can populate Menu.KeyBindings for their own key lifecycle.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.MenuOptions.ConfirmExit</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native menu hosts may change the unsaved-change exit-confirmation policy; Show-ConsoleMenu deliberately retains the default confirmation.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleMenu with its normal unsaved-change protection; set ConfirmExit in a native menu host when a different policy is required.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.MenuOptions.SidebarMinimumWidth</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native menu hosts may tune the Shell sidebar breakpoint; Show-ConsoleMenu exposes the layout choice and keeps the 84-column breakpoint.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleMenu -Layout Auto/Classic/Shell/Inline; native MenuOptions.SidebarMinimumWidth controls a custom breakpoint.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Interactive.PromptLabels.ActionOutput</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native prompt hosts can replace the 'Action output · Alt+PgUp/PgDn scroll' caption (The action output pane's title while idle.) independently of the language catalogue; PowerShell retains its built-in translated wording.</td><td>Select the Prompt.ActionOutput catalogue entry through CONSOLEMONSTER_LANGUAGE or $PSUICulture; use Title/Description for question-specific wording.</td></tr>

Start-ConsoleRun creates its own session and selects host-safe capture/output before LiveRun fixes inline sizing, cancellation and its summary.</td><td>Use Start-ConsoleRun high-level live/progress/height options and Complete-ConsoleRun; native LiveRunOptions.Session is the embedding-host extension point.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.AutoRecordFolder</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose a separate automatic-recording directory. Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -AutoRecord uses the platform recording directory and does not expose a second storage path.</td><td>Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -RecordingPath for an explicit file, or -AutoRecord for the standard folder.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.AutoRecordMaxBytes</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose the automatic-recording retention budget. The PowerShell dashboard retains the bounded 50-MB default alongside its AutoRecord count.</td><td>Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -AutoRecord for retention count, or -RecordingPath for a caller-owned recording file.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.CaptureConsole</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native session hosts decide whether to intercept Console.Out/Error. Start-ConsoleRun selects capture from the owning PowerShell host and uses a host queue when raw console capture would break that host.</td><td>Use Start-ConsoleRun/Invoke-ConsoleDashboard and their normal PowerShell stream routing; native sessions may set CaptureConsole explicitly.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Culture</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can pin one session's numeric/date culture. The PowerShell session keeps the detected profile culture instead of a per-session culture object.</td><td>Select the current culture or CONSOLEMONSTER_CULTURE for the host; native LiveSessionOptions.Culture can override one session.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Discoverable</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose whether LiveSession.Current exposes a run to other operations. Start-ConsoleRun deliberately sets false so tracked work does not capture unrelated updates or prompts.</td><td>Update the returned run handle with Update-Console -Run; Invoke-ConsoleDashboard retains its normal discoverable dashboard scope.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.HandleCancelKey</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native sessions choose whether to intercept Console.CancelKeyPress. Watch-Console disables this interception and uses PowerShell StopProcessing for Ctrl+C.</td><td>Use the high-level command's normal PowerShell cancellation; native LiveSessionOptions.HandleCancelKey configures console-host interception.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.LogTarget</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native sessions may direct captured output to a particular log widget. LiveRun chooses its own dashboard log and ordinary dashboards discover the log target when this option is null.</td><td>Compose a log region in the dashboard or use Start-ConsoleRun's managed log; native hosts can select a LogTarget explicitly.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.NotifyOnFinish</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native session hosts can enable the completion bell. PowerShell leaves the optional bell disabled rather than adding a command-level notification policy.</td><td>Use normal command completion and its final summary; native LiveSessionOptions.NotifyOnFinish enables a completion bell.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Output</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can lend an ITerminalOutput whose lifetime they own. The PowerShell dashboard selects a host queue/output implementation for jobs, remoting, transcripts and redirected output.</td><td>Use Use-ConsoleTarget for supported scoped output; the high-level live command owns its terminal-output lifecycle.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Profile</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts may override a single session's terminal capabilities. PowerShell detects its current host and applies a plain host profile where direct terminal output is unsafe.</td><td>Use the detected host profile and high-level -NoLive; native LiveSessionOptions.Profile supplies a custom session profile.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.RecordingName</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose the automatic-recording filename prefix. Invoke-ConsoleDashboard deliberately uses dashboard for its automatic recordings.</td><td>Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -RecordingPath to name a file, or -AutoRecord for the dashboard-prefixed automatic series.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.RecordWriter</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can lend an event-recording TextWriter that is flushed but left open. The PowerShell dashboard exposes an owned recording path, not a borrowed event sink.</td><td>Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -RecordingPath; native LiveSessionOptions.RecordWriter supports a caller-owned writer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.ReplayDelay</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native replay hosts can supply deterministic timing and cancellation handling. Show-ConsoleReplay exposes playback Speed and uses the normal replay delay implementation.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleReplay -Speed/-PlaybackMode; native replay fixtures can provide LiveSessionOptions.ReplayDelay.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StopOnCancellation</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts choose whether rendering stops immediately or drains until Stop. LiveRun deliberately sets false so completed worker results can reach the final summary.</td><td>Use Complete-ConsoleRun in finally and normal command cancellation; native sessions may choose their own drain policy.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StopTimeout</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts set the render-thread join timeout. PowerShell commands retain the session's bounded two-second stop wait and own their finally/disposal path.</td><td>Use the high-level command's cancellation and cleanup; native LiveSessionOptions.StopTimeout tunes a custom host's render-thread join.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StreamHeartbeat</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native sessions tune append-only summary heartbeats. LiveRun disables the session heartbeat and owns its separate count/time progress triggers.</td><td>Use Start-ConsoleRun -ProgressEvery/-ProgressIntervalSeconds for run progress, or native StreamHeartbeat for a standalone session.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.StreamTimestamps</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can override append-only narration timestamps. PowerShell retains automatic CI-profile detection instead of adding another timestamp switch to live commands.</td><td>Use the host's normal CI-aware narration; native LiveSessionOptions.StreamTimestamps forces the per-session timestamp policy.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Target</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can override one session's ITerminalTarget independently of the ambient target. PowerShell scopes the target and preserves high-level session ownership.</td><td>Use Use-ConsoleTarget -Target/-Path/-Writer around the command; native LiveSessionOptions.Target overrides a single session.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.TaskbarProgress</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts may disable the terminal/taskbar progress indicator. PowerShell retains the default automatic progress reporting and reset at session completion.</td><td>Use the normal live dashboard progress lifecycle; native LiveSessionOptions.TaskbarProgress changes the terminal-indicator policy.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.LiveSessionOptions.Theme</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native hosts can override one session's ITheme independently of Terminal.Theme. The PowerShell live commands use the selected ambient theme.</td><td>Use Set-ConsoleTheme for the supported host theme; native LiveSessionOptions.Theme overrides one session.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Live.WatchOptions.Session</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native watch hosts can supply an exclusive LiveSessionOptions instance. Watch-Console owns an inline session, final-state retention and cancellation through StopProcessing.</td><td>Use Watch-Console -NoLive/-PollIntervalSeconds/-Count; native WatchOptions.Session configures a custom watch host.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Force</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: A native output adapter may force registered-view rendering outside direct console output. The installed PowerShell adapter supplies verified provenance and explicit Show commands select views directly.</td><td>Use Show-Console or Enable-ConsoleFormatting; custom native output hosts can configure ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Force.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.HelpSink</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The native adapter supplies the actual help-producing PSCmdlet after checking its provenance. Accepting it from a script would not establish trusted help-output routing.</td><td>Use native Get-Help with ConsoleMonster help formatting enabled; a native host must provide its verified help sink.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Shim</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The native adapter marks its invocation as the installed default-output shim so only enabled formatting features run. This is adapter provenance, not a user formatting choice.</td><td>Use Enable-ConsoleFormatting -Include/-Exclude; the installed adapter supplies Shim internally.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.TopLevel</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The native adapter establishes whether the sink belongs to a top-level submission before displaying automatic views and errors. A script flag cannot establish that pipeline provenance.</td><td>Use normal direct console output or an explicit Show command; the adapter determines TopLevel.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.PowerShell.ConsoleDefaultOutputOptions.Transcript</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: The native adapter preserves PowerShell's transcript routing and uses native Out-Default -Transcript when needed. Scripts do not choose this verified routing state.</td><td>Use PowerShell's normal Start-Transcript/Stop-Transcript lifecycle; the adapter supplies Transcript.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Replay.ReplayOptions.Interactive</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native replay hosts may inject interactive devices, labels and targets. Show-ConsoleReplay builds host-aware PSInteractive options and supplies the owning host line console when needed.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleReplay -PlaybackMode/-Paused and the normal host; native ReplayOptions.Interactive supports custom devices.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Replay.ReplayOptions.Session</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native automatic-replay hosts may inject session output and deterministic delay. Show-ConsoleReplay owns its automatic-playback session and exposes playback controls rather than a nested session object.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleReplay -PlaybackMode Automatic/-Speed/-Inline; native ReplayOptions.Session configures a custom replay host.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Sessions.SessionRecordingOptions.Folder</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native recorders can change the directory used for automatically generated cast names. Invoke-ConsoleRecording exposes the exact recording file and retains the standard default directory when omitted.</td><td>Use Invoke-ConsoleRecording -RecordingPath to choose the complete cast path; native SessionRecordingOptions.Folder changes automatic naming location.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.Alignment</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native view builders can configure an embedded rule's alignment. Show-Console no longer owns the rule hierarchy/view job; the rule constructor retains its alignment contract.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleRule -Alignment and render the resulting widget, or configure ConsoleViewOptions.Alignment in native view code.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Views.ConsoleViewOptions.ChildrenProperty</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native view builders can select a named hierarchy child member. Show-Console -View Tree now uses object inspection; explicit hierarchy construction belongs to New-ConsoleTree.</td><td>Use New-ConsoleTree -ChildrenProperty for a named child-member hierarchy, or Show-Console -View Tree for object inspection.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.FixedSlots</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native app footers can reserve a slot for every command and shorten labels. Show-ConsoleApp -FooterHints builds the ordinary adaptive hint list.</td><td>Use -FooterHints for the supported hint layout; pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer for native fixed-slot composition.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.HintsSource</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native app registries can supply render-time hints for the current focus/dialog. The PowerShell hint parameter is a concrete hint sequence and does not turn a scriptblock into a render-thread callback.</td><td>Use -FooterHints for fixed hints, or pass a typed FooterBar with a thread-safe native HintsSource through -Footer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Indent</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native footer composition can change its first drawing column. The PowerShell built-in footer retains the standard one-cell inset.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleApp -FooterHints for the standard inset, or pass a configured FooterBar through -Footer.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.KeepLast</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native footers can preserve a final help/key-map hint when earlier hints overflow. The PowerShell footer keeps the standard adaptive list policy.</td><td>Choose the -FooterHints sequence for ordinary hints, or pass a configured FooterBar through -Footer for custom overflow retention.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Message</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native toast hosts can replace hints with a styled message line. PowerShell -FooterHints defines hints rather than a transient toast state.</td><td>Pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer for native message-state composition.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Right</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native footer composition can add a styled right-hand line independently of hints. The PowerShell hint shorthand owns only the hint sequence.</td><td>Pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer when a separate right-hand line is required.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.FooterBar.Segments</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native footers can add right-hand linked/tinted metadata segments. The PowerShell hint shorthand does not construct FooterSegment records.</td><td>Pass a configured FooterBar through Show-ConsoleApp -Footer for native linked-segment composition.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.HeaderBar.Crumbs</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native menu/form runners generate breadcrumb steps from their navigation stack; the Show-ConsoleApp header shorthand exposes title/subtitle rather than an independent breadcrumb collection.</td><td>Use menu/submenu navigation for generated breadcrumbs, or compose a typed HeaderBar in Show-ConsoleApp -Content.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.HeaderBar.Elapsed</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native header hosts can pin the clock value instead of the render context clock. PowerShell dashboards use the session clock and do not expose a second header clock.</td><td>Use Invoke-ConsoleDashboard -Clock for a deterministic session clock, or compose a typed HeaderBar for an independent clock value.</td></tr>
<tr><td><code>ConsoleMonster.Widgets.HeaderBar.HeaderRight</code></td><td>CSharpOnly: Native grid/menu/form runners add contextual row/step captions to the header. The Show-ConsoleApp shorthand keeps its supported title/subtitle/detail/status fields.</td><td>Use Show-ConsoleApp -Detail/-Status for its status area, or compose a typed HeaderBar in -Content for independent right-hand text.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>

## .NET host integrations

The PowerShell formatting, help and progress examples run inside a compiled PSCmdlet on its owning pipeline thread. The generic-host and ILogger examples configure .NET lifetimes; their PowerShell tab launches the same project. These options remain explicit C# integration settings.
